answers.answer: Open Settings, then Spam defense in the Access group. The page shows one card per group, and you can change every setting in those groups: Master, Trust, New accounts and new followers, Message content, Coordinated campaigns, Sudden activity, Raid lockdown and Shared spam list. Change a number or flip a switch, then choose Save. Six settings carry Not yet active: the join rate, the three lockdown settings and two shared-list switches. Their values are saved but have no effect, except that the lockdown values apply to a lockdown started by hand.
answers.quote: The page shows one card for each group of settings.

answers.answer: You need to be signed in to the channel. You must be the Broadcaster, or a person the Broadcaster has given the permit to manage the spam policy; other roles can only read the values. This is stated in the 'Who can use this page' table and in the note about the Save button.
answers.quote: The Save button shows only to someone who may change the page.

answers.answer: After an edit, the header shows 'Unsaved changes' and Save becomes active. After you choose Save, the bot shows 'Spam defense saved.' A value out of range keeps Save inactive, and most settings show the reason in red.
answers.quote: The bot stores every setting at once and shows “Spam defense saved.”

answers.answer: Save stays inactive until a value changes, and the watch-only switch already shows on. So the streamer cannot save watch-only mode by itself before any other change. They change one value, for example the threshold, and then choose Save. That one save stores every setting, including watch-only as on, which also stops the viewer-selling exception.
answers.quote: So change any other value first, for example one threshold, and then choose Save.

answers.answer: Only after reading the Trust table do I learn that the fourth established threshold is saved but has no effect. A reader who has already changed it to delay trust learns too late that the change did nothing.
answers.quote: Strike-free days before a viewer counts as established is saved, but the current spam-defense calculation assumes the viewer has no recent upheld strike instead of checking their moderation history.

answers.answer: The paragraph explaining that the label says one tier but the setting uses another makes a listener hold two tier names at once. I reread it to be sure which viewers are affected.
answers.quote: The setting’s label says established viewers, but its actual alphabet threshold is the Regular tier.

The six short sentences each state a default, a consequence or a step in order. The workaround (change one other value, then Save) is what the application case needs, and it arrives in sequence.

The five sentences describe what exoneration undoes. The closing sentence about keeping thresholds apart is loose, but the ordering rule it refers to is spelled out in the list below, so the cost to the reader is small.
